attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Answers

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16) — refreshes S3 presigned URLs for attachments whose `LastPresignedTime` is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days), `runner.go:43` `RunOnce` → `CheckAndPresign` (`runner.go:47`) — schedule: once eagerly at startup, then every 12 hours via `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27, ticker at :30) — wiring: `Server.startBackgroundRunners`, server/server.go:162-171 (eager `RunOnce` at server/server.go:163, goroutine `Run` at :169), called from `Server.Start` server/server.go:129.

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120 (HTTP POST executed at internal/webhook/webhook.go:152 via `safeClient.Do`); async path `webhook.PostAsync` (internal/webhook/webhook.go:184) enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue` (:39) drained by 4 goroutines started in `init` (:42-54), which also call `Post`.
Protection: SSRF guard at dial time — `safeDialContext` (internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-76) installed as the shared client's `Transport.DialContext` (internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37); it resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` (internal/webhook/validate.go:44) against `reservedCIDRs` (internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23: loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents). Because the check happens after resolution at dial time, it also defeats DNS rebinding. Additionally `webhook.ValidateURL` (internal/webhook/validate.go:65) pre-validates scheme + resolved IPs at webhook-registration time, and `AllowPrivateIPs` (internal/webhook/validate.go:41) can disable the guard for self-hosted setups.

**h03** — abstraction package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp` (internal/idp/idp.go — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the shared user-info contract); implementation package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2` (internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20 `IdentityProvider`, :27 `NewIdentityProvider`, :47 `ExchangeToken`, :83 `UserInfo`). OAuth2 (with PKCE) is the only concrete protocol shipped; both are consumed at server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:12-13.

**h04** — no. Evidence: the only import of `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql` in the whole repo is store/db/db.go:8, and the only call to `mysql.NewDB` is the factory switch at store/db/db.go:22. (`grep -rn "store/db/mysql" --include=*.go .` returns exactly that one line; the `mysql.*` hits in store/test/containers.go:101-105 are the `testcontainers-go/modules/mysql` package, not the memos driver.) Tests reach the driver only through `db.NewDBDriver` (store/test/store.go:28,50).

**h05** — mechanism: explicit Go code inside the delete-user transaction; there is no DB-level cascade for reactions. Evidence:
- `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (deletes reactions *on* the user's memos) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (deletes reactions *authored by* the user) are called at store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96 and :102 (declared at :380 and :400); identical code at store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102 and store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102.
- Entry points: `Store.DeleteUser` store/user.go:171 → `driver.DeleteUser` → `(*DB).DeleteUser` store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29 → `deleteUserTargetsTx` :90.
- No FK/cascade exists: the `reaction` table is declared with no FOREIGN KEY at store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99, store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98, store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql (and originally store/migration/*/0.20/00__reaction.sql). The only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in current schema is `memo_share.memo_id` (store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109).

**h06** — handlers (all in server/router/api/v1):
- `CreateMemo` — memo_service.go:70 → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at :157
- `UpdateMemo` — memo_service.go:401 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at :513 → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (memo_update_helpers.go:67)
- `DeleteMemo` — memo_service.go:518 → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at :562
- `CreateMemoComment` — memo_service_comments.go:20 → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at :119
- `SetMemoAttachments` — memo_attachment_service.go:16 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at :48
- `SetMemoRelations` — memo_relation_service.go:16 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at :48

Convergence: all four `Dispatch*Webhook` methods funnel into `webhook.PostAsync` (memo_service_webhooks.go:43 and :71), and the actual outbound request is made in the single function `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120. - `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
